research_method.nlm: Repository mining / ML / quantitative; rolling time-window feature extraction, composite proxy score Bd, supervised classification (ANN best of ten models), React-Vite dashboard with LLM-based natural language interface
research_method.value: Repository mining of the 20-MAD dataset (Jira issues merged with GitHub commits, rolling time-window features); supervised ML classification of a theory-informed composite burnout-risk proxy label (Bd = 0.35W + 0.25I + 0.25C + 0.15X, threshold 0.5); ten classifiers compared (stratified 70-30 split, five-fold cross-validation; ANN best); Spearman correlation of predictors; dashboard prototype with LLM-based natural language interface
research_method.note: Split and cross-validation details reported only by Claude (not contradicted).

evidence.quote: This historical dataset contains issue-tracking data from Jira and code activity data from GitHub, for several Apache projects, including Hadoop, HDFS, and Zookeeper.
Thus, this research reflects as an initial repository-based evaluation of a multimodal burnout prediction framework rather than a direct study of industrial Scrum/Kanban teams.
a theory-informed proxy measure of burnout risk was developed based on four workrelated dimensions, such as workload intensity, irregular working patterns, task complexity, and context-switching.
Five-fold cross-validation was used to ensure robustness and minimize overfitting.
An LLM architecture based natural language interface was developed and integrated into the dashboard, allowing stakeholders to query the system whenever necessary.
Several machine learning models were trained and evaluated for predicting developer burnout. Among all the trained models, Artificial Neural Network (ANN) revealed superior predictive performance
Among all predictors, commits count showed the strongest positive association with burnout risk by obtaining a Spearman correlation coefficient (ρ) of 0.519.
other significant indicators of burnout include total lines changed (ρ = 0.486), and issues handled in the backlog of Jira (ρ = 0.454)
